headline: Microsoft chief executive Satya Nadella argued that AI agents make business software more important, not less, and that Microsoft wants Copilot to become the operating system for work.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a major CEO's view on the AI-versus-software debate, but largely a company pitch.
importance_line: Business customers and software makers are affected, but this is Microsoft's own claim about its products, and GitHub's activity figures are not independently checked.
summary: The Times of India reports that Nadella wrote in an X post that AI is changing work so that software is organised around tasks instead of people working around software, citing rising repository creation, pull requests (proposed code changes) and commits on GitHub as a sign that more agents make trusted record-keeping systems more important. He tied this to Microsoft's announcement of more than 30 new Copilot skills in its Dynamics 365 business apps and a managed runtime that lets code run inside a company's own environment, which are Microsoft's own claims and plans.
notes: Times of India summarises a Nadella X post; the post itself was not opened.
